fixes.fix_explanation: A sitemap.xml file helps search engines discover and index all your important pages efficiently. Submit this to Google Search Console and Bing Webmaster Tools.
fixes.fix_location: Save as /sitemap.xml in the website root directory, then reference it in robots.txt.

fixes.fix_explanation: A robots.txt file tells search engine crawlers which pages they can access and where to find your sitemap. This configuration allows all crawlers to access your entire site.
fixes.fix_location: Save as /robots.txt in the website root directory.

fixes.fix_code:
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Organization",
  "name": "The Daily Grind",
  "url": "https://example-blog.com/",
  "logo": "https://example-blog.com/logo.png",
  "description": "Explore the world of specialty coffee. Brewing guides, bean reviews, and café culture from around the globe.",
  "sameAs": [
    "https://twitter.com/dailygrindcoffee",
    "https://instagram.com/dailygrindcoffee"
  ]
}
</script>
fixes.fix_explanation: JSON-LD structured data helps search engines understand your content and can enable rich snippets in search results. This Organization schema identifies your brand to Google.
fixes.fix_location: Paste inside the <head> section, after the existing meta tags and before </head>.
